## Summary

I refactored `extra/viz/cli.py` to make the profiling CLI testable:

1. **`get_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser`** — Extracted the parser construction (previously inline in the `if __name__ == "__main__"` block) into a public, importable function. It returns a parser supporting `--profile`, `--profile-path`, `--device` (plus the existing `--rewrites`, `--kernel`, `--no-color`, `--select`, `--rewrites-path`).

2. **`main(args) -> None`** — Changed the signature from `main()` (which read a global `args`) to `main(args)` accepting a parsed namespace. Replaced all three `sys.exit(0)` calls inside `main` (device listing, SQTT printer, profiler printer) with plain `return`, so callers can capture stdout and continue.

3. **`__main__` block** — Now just calls `parser = get_arg_parser()`, parses, and invokes `main(args)`. Its own `sys.exit(0)` (help path) stays, since it's outside `main`.

Behavior is preserved: the device-listing path still prints available device names (including `SQTT` counter names built from `counters`), and the SQTT path still prints the `Clk` header, a separator line, then per-event rows whose first token is the integer clock timestamp `int(e.st)`.

Verified the module imports cleanly and the parser/namespace round-trips as expected. I did not touch anything under `test/`.
